description: Product-supported FFmpeg capabilities (PRD FR-3). Source of truth for what fass may build. Actual encoder/filter/muxer availability depends on the installed FFmpeg build — check with `fass env` or `--preflight`.

tested_ffmpeg.builds: Ubuntu 24.04 package (6.1.1-3ubuntu5) and jrottenberg/ffmpeg:9.0-nvidia2404 (9.0.1) — both carry every encoder and muxer in this registry (the 6.1.1 build lacks the standalone AAC/ADTS muxer; preflight reports it)
tested_ffmpeg.notes: libx264, libhevc, libvpx-vp9, libmp3lame, libvorbis, libopus, prores_ks, mpeg2video, mpeg4, mjpeg, gif, libwebp, mp2, ac3, eac3, alac, flac, pcm_*, dvvideo verified present on both

hls.note: playlist + segment files, written into the output directory; -f hls is always emitted explicitly

mxf.note: broadcast master wrapper (OP-Atom) — the muxer takes an encoded master: video is re-encoded into it (stream-copied h264 arrives avcc-packaged and the mxf muxer rejects it), audio must be PCM, and the h264 GOP is capped (ffmpeg 9.x's mxf index table requires frame offsets within ±127)

aac.note: audio only, ADTS framing — the muxer's name in FFmpeg is 'adts' (the 'aac' format entry is demux-only)

srt_file.note: subtitle dump file (distinct from the srt:// streaming protocol)

h264.requires: libx264 — present in nearly all builds

h265.requires: libhevc — built into FFmpeg, but encoding is slower
h265.note: Smaller files than H.264 at similar quality; slower to encode.

prores.note: Apple ProRes — 10-bit mastering/archive codec. Quality is set by the encoder profile (proxy/lt/standard/hq/4444/4444xq), not a quality preset; files are large.

mpeg2.note: MPEG-2 — broadcast / DVD / VOB material. Bitrate-targeted (no CRF).

mpeg4.requires: mpeg4 (MPEG-4 Part 2) — native encoder, built in
mpeg4.note: Legacy MPEG-4 Part 2 — classic AVI/WMV material.

dv.note: DV (PAL/NTSC DV camcorder standard), SD only.

gif.note: Animated GIF: 256 colors, no audio. Keep durations short.

gpu.description: NVIDIA GPU encoding (M6). When plan.output.gpu is true the video encoder switches to the nvenc coder for the requested codec: h264 -> h264_nvenc, h265 -> hevc_nvenc. Every other codec (VP9, ProRes, MPEG-2, …) is CPU-only and rejected. Audio is always CPU-encoded — nvenc carries video only. The deployment must expose a GPU (docker --gpus / compose device reservation; see the gpu block of the deployment config).

constraints.vp9: VP9 encoding is CPU-only (libvpx-vp9) — GPU is not available for it
constraints.other_codecs: ProRes, MPEG-2, MPEG-4, MJPEG, DV, GIF and WebP are CPU-only (no nvenc coder)
constraints.video_preset: x264 speed presets (ultrafast..veryslow) are x264-specific and do not apply to nvenc
constraints.video_profile: nvenc supports the 'main' and 'high' profiles only; 'baseline' has no nvenc form
constraints.bitrate: a target video bitrate works unchanged: -b:v/-maxrate (nvenc's CBR-style target)
constraints.pixel_format: yuv420p and yuv420p10le are supported by both nvenc coders

mp2.note: MPEG-1/2 Layer II — the classic broadcast MPEG-TS audio

alac.note: Apple Lossless — lossless, no bitrate flag

audio_container_for_codec.description: When an audio-only output names a codec but no container, this is the natural file format for it.

rtsp.stream_only_note: output only to an rtsp(s):// destination; never a file

srt.stream_only_note: output only to an srt:// destination; never a file

hls.note: HLS: .m3u8 playlist + transport segments in the output directory; tune with hls_* format options

mxf.note: MXF is a broadcast master format: audio must be PCM (the mxf muxer rejects aac/ac3), and the video is re-encoded into it even when the codec matches

webp.note: the muxer has no audio path in the MVP — audio is dropped

streaming.description: Stream / remote I/O (M3b + protocol expansion). Inputs may be URLs with an allowlisted scheme (they are read by the user's local ffmpeg — fass never fetches or executes); outputs may be stream destinations. rtmp/rtmps/rtsp/rtsps/srt/udp/rtp/tcp have a fixed container; http/https derive the container from the URL path extension (.mp4 → mp4, .ts → mpegts, .m3u8 → hls, .mp3 → mp3, …) defaulting to mpegts, which is what HTTP live pushing conventionally carries. Everything stays an argv token; stream destinations are disclosed in the explanation.
streaming.note: Scheme defaults come from https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-formats.html (rtmp->flv, rtsp->rtsp, udp/rtp/tcp->mpegts); fass still emits an explicit -f for stream destinations. HTTP output uploads the encoded stream to the endpoint (the server must accept the PUT/POST upload).

format_options.description: Output-side container/format options (https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-formats.html#Format-Options). Each key is a valid '-<key> value' pair on the output command; the plan carries them as output.format_options {key: value} and the executor validates every key/value against this table before spawning a process. 'kind' drives validation: rate (e.g. 1000k / 1000000), number (seconds, may be negative), int, bool (0/1), choice (one of values), flagset ('+'-joined flags, each optionally prefixed with +/-), metadata (key=value pairs), brand (4 lowercase alphanumerics), url.

limit_rate.description: maximum rate ffmpeg may use to read the input (streaming)

metadata.description: write metadata tags, e.g. 'title=My Clip, comment=made with fass'

map_metadata.description: map metadata from global/input 0/1 to global/input 0/1; -1 disables

start_time.description: set the start timestamp of the output (seconds)

output_ts_offset.description: offset the output timestamps (seconds, may be negative)

pkt_timebase.description: packet timebase to write into the container

avoid_negative_ts.description: how the muxer deals with negative timestamps

muxer_queue_size.description: max number of packets queued for muxing

max_muxing_queue_size.description: max packets buffered per stream before dropping input frames

flush_packets.description: flush the stream at each muxing step (streaming)

reserve.description: reserve space for the index (MP4/ASF, e.g. old QuickTime compatibility)

movflags.description: MP4/MOV/M4A file flags, '+'-joined with optional +/- prefix (faststart = move the index up front for web playback)

brand.description: override the MP4/MOV/3GP major brand, e.g. 'isom'

max_bpf.description: max bytes per packet (MP4 fragment interleaving)

write_btrt.description: write the btrt MP4 atom even when values are 0

write_tmcd.description: write a tmcd atom with the specified timecode start

ctts_delta.description: force creation or suppression of the ctts atom

use_metadata_tags.description: use new-style metadata tags instead of XMP

frag_duration.description: target duration (seconds) of fragmented-MP4 fragments (live streaming)

frag_interval.description: force a new fragment at least every N seconds

frag_every_key.description: start a new fragment at every keyframe

empty_moov.description: write an empty moov atom up front (fragmented MP4 live)

separate_moof.description: write each moof into its own file (DASH segmenting)

mpegts_flags.description: MPEG-TS muxer flags, '+'-joined with optional +/- prefix (resend_headers re-writes program headers periodically; mpeg2 uses MPEG-2 framing)

mpegts_pmt_start_pid.description: first PID used in the PMT

mpegts_start_pid.description: first PID assigned to the streams

mpegts_m2ts_mode.description: use the M2TS variant of the framing

hls_flags.description: HLS behavior flags, comma-joined (split_by_time cuts on the wall clock, not keyframes)

hls_playlist_type.description: playlist type: event (live) or vod (finished, full list)

hls_allow_cache.description: allow clients to cache segments (1) or not (0)

hls_base_url.description: URL prefix prepended to playlist entries

hls_segment_size.description: max segment size in bytes (0 = unlimited)

use_odml.description: write the ODML (Open DML) chunk for large AVI files

flvflags.description: FLV file flags, comma-joined (no_duration omits the duration in the header — live)

write_id3v1.description: also write an ID3v1 tag (old players)

write_xing.description: write a Xing/Info header (duration) into the WAV file

filters.description: Allowlisted FFmpeg filters (https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-filters.html). The NLU may name these (FilterOp expr / plan.filtergraph); every filter instance in a graph is validated against this table — name, domain and argument characters — before a process is spawned. Filters that open files or devices beyond the plan's own inputs (movie=, avfilter sources, …) are deliberately absent from the allowlist.

drawtext.description: burn in text: 'drawtext=text=hi:x=10:y=10:fontsize=24:fontcolor=white'; 'drawtext=timestamp=localtime:x=10:y=10' for a timecode

split.description: split the stream into N copies (graph filter): 'split=2'

subtitles.description: burn in a subtitle file: 'subtitles=file.srt' (path needs filter escaping)

atempo.description: playback speed 0.5-2.0 per instance (chain for more)

bitrate_policy: An explicit target video bitrate (plan.output.video_bitrate_kbps) overrides the quality preset: -b:v and -maxrate at the target, plus -bufsize at 2x the target for H.264/H.265 (a CBR-style target; audio keeps its codec-preset bitrate). An explicit audio bitrate (plan.output.audio_bitrate_kbps) overrides the codec preset's -b:a; lossless/PCM codecs (flac, alac, pcm_*) take no bitrate flag and a requested one is reported as a note.

pixel_formats.description: Output pixel formats per video codec (the scaling/pixel-format-conversion component). The codec's video_codecs[*].pix_fmt is the default; yuv420p10le is the 10-bit form, yuv444p full chroma (VP9), yuvj420p full-range 8-bit (MJPEG), yuv422p10le/yuv444p10le are the ProRes forms, rgb24/yuva420p for GIF/WebP.

video_profiles.description: Encoder profiles: H.264 'baseline' maximizes compatibility with old players; ProRes profiles select the ProRes family (proxy..4444xq).

video_presets.description: x264 speed/quality trade-off presets (H.264 only; libhevc/libvpx-vp9 and the other codecs do not use x264 presets and are not exposed).

audio_resample.description: Audio resampler targets: -ar sample rate (Hz) and -ac channel count (1 mono, 2 stereo, 6 5.1).

speed.description: Playback-speed change: setpts=PTS/factor on video, an atempo chain on audio (atempo accepts 0.5-2.0 per instance, so larger factors chain instances). For audio-only output the atempo chain is the only speed mechanism (no setpts).

crop.description: Crop to exact output dimensions, centered (FFmpeg's crop default).

bitstream_filters.description: Stream-copy (remux) bitstream filters. When remuxing from an MP4/MOV container to MPEG-TS, H.264/HEVC must be restamped into Annex-B form; when remuxing AAC audio out of MPEG-TS into MP4/MOV, the ADTS header must be stripped. Filters run on the compressed stream only, without re-encoding. For audio-only copy (extracting an audio track), the same AAC rule applies: AAC in MPEG-TS is ADTS-framed, MP4/MOV/M4A need the header stripped.

sources.description: Generic ffmpeg input sources (the input/output-devices component). An asset whose path is '<format>:<spec>' with an allowlisted format is a source spec, not a file: it gets -f <format> plus ;key=value options as separate option tokens. Output devices carry audio only (pcm) — a plan that produces video cannot target one.

resize.description: Scale the video. A height (e.g. 720p) or width keeps the aspect ratio; width+height letterboxes (preserve) or stretches (exact).
resize.note: A 720p request sets the output height to 720 with an aspect-compatible even width — it does not pad or crop to 1280x720.

grayscale.description: Remove color from the video (black and white). Audio is unaffected.

watermark.description: Overlay one static image throughout the output.
watermark.note: Image is shown at original size unless scaled; margin is in output pixels; the overlay persists for the whole interval (single-frame input never bounds duration).

audio_replace.description: Replace the output audio with the first audio stream of another input (an audio file).
audio_replace.note: Emits -map N:a:0 for the replacement input plus -shortest, so the output ends when the shorter of the video and the replacement audio ends. The replacement audio is encoded to the container's audio codec (no stream copy).

crop.description: Crop to exact output dimensions, centered (FFmpeg's crop default).
crop.note: Width/height snap to even (yuv420p); the planner rejects a crop larger than the probed source dimensions.

speed.audio: -af atempo chain (0.5-2.0 per instance, chained for larger factors)
speed.note: A trim's source duration is divided by the factor; the output is shorter than the cut interval. Audio-only output uses the atempo chain alone.

rotate.description: Rotate by a quarter turn (90/180/270; clockwise by default).
rotate.filter: transpose=1 (90 CW), transpose=2 (90 CCW / 270 CW), hflip+vflip (180)

audio_resample.description: Resample the audio to a target sample rate and/or channel count.
audio_resample.note: Targets come from the audio_resample matrix.

subtitles.description: Add subtitles from a bound subtitle file (srt/ass/ssa/vtt), burned in (default) or as a selectable track.
subtitles.filter: subtitles= (srt/vtt) / ass= (ass/ssa) for burn; -map N:s:0 + -c:s for soft
subtitles.note: See the top-level 'subtitles' block: burn forces a re-encode, soft muxes mov_text (mp4/mov) or srt (mkv) and is copy-compatible. At most one subtitle operation per plan; the subtitle asset is bound outside the model.

filter.description: Apply an FFmpeg filter by expression (a single filter instance or a comma-joined chain of same-domain filters), from the registry 'filters' allowlist: video filters (eq=, fade=, drawtext=, boxblur=, unsharp=, volume-like audio filters go to domain audio …), e.g. {"type": "filter", "domain": "video", "expr": "eq=contrast=1.2"} or {"type": "filter", "domain": "audio", "expr": "loudnorm"}. The whole expression is validated against the allowlist; anything else is rejected.
filter.note: Raw FFmpeg filter syntax, allowlist-validated. A full labeled graph (multiple outputs, audio+video in one graph) goes to plan.filtergraph instead — it cannot be combined with a watermark or burned subtitles, which own the filter graph.

subtitles.description: Subtitle support (the subtitles/demuxer-encoder component). Subtitles arrive as a typed asset (srt/ass/ssa/vtt) and are either burned into the video (hard-coded, libass) or muxed as a selectable track (soft). The input's own subtitle tracks can also be DUMPED to a file: output mode "subtitles" with a srt_file/vtt_file/ass_file container emits -map 0:s:0 -c:s <codec>.
subtitles.note: burn uses the libass filters 'subtitles=' (srt/vtt) or 'ass=' (ass/ssa) in the video filter chain and forces a video re-encode; the filename needs two layers of FFmpeg filter escaping (graph parser, then filter-option parser). soft muxes a selectable track: mp4/mov → mov_text, mkv → srt (encoded from the source format); other containers (webm, mpegts, flv, rtsp, srt) have no soft-subtitle codec and soft mode is rejected there. soft mode never forces a video re-encode — it is compatible with -c copy. dump (mode "subtitles") writes the input's first subtitle stream to a .srt/.vtt/.ass file: -map 0:s:0 -c:s srt|webvtt|ass. Filenames containing ':' cannot be handled by FFmpeg at all (its URL layer parses them as a protocol); the planner rejects them with a clear error. No -shortest: subtitles may legitimately be shorter or longer than the video.

stream_selection.audio: 0:a:0 (first audio stream only; additional streams are excluded). With audio_replace, the mapped audio stream is the first audio stream of the replacement input instead.
stream_selection.note: Additional streams beyond the first video and first audio are not carried over (visible notice in the explanation). Subtitle streams are the exception only when a soft-subtitle operation is present (first subtitle stream of the subtitle asset mapped) or the output mode is 'subtitles' (the first subtitle stream of the INPUT is dumped). Audio-only output maps 0:a:0 exclusively.

trim_policy: Trimming re-encodes: the MVP prioritizes accurate cuts over fast stream-copy cuts (PRD FR-4).
copy_policy: Stream copy (remux) is chosen only when no filters are required AND media metadata proves the input streams already match the requested codecs. Without metadata the planner re-encodes and says so. Audio-only output copies the source audio codec when the metadata proves it matches the requested audio codec (e.g. 'extract the audio' from an AAC file to M4A); otherwise it re-encodes. Soft subtitles are compatible with copy (mapped with -map N:s:0 and encoded with -c:s, overriding -c copy for that stream only); burning subtitles is a filter and forces a re-encode.
